justification: The system's operational robustness is supported by extensive evidence of its behavior across various non-nominal conditions. These include testing with randomly removed non-critical fields (93.7% accuracy), OCR degradation (92.1% accuracy), formatting variations (91.6% to 94.8% accuracy), and three predefined perturbation tests (92.8%, 90.9%, and 93.4%). Additionally, an out-of-distribution mechanism successfully flagged 1,127 out of 1,200 (approx. 94%) OOD documents from excluded classes. This wide-ranging evaluation beyond nominal conditions, which was also independently reproduced, satisfies the criteria for demonstrating operational robustness.
evidence_used: With 10% randomly removed non-critical fields, accuracy was 93.7%.
With the predefined OCR degradation transformation, accuracy was 92.1%.
Across the predefined formatting-variation set, accuracy ranged from 91.6% to 94.8%.
Of the 1,200 out-of-distribution samples, 1,127 were flagged by the out-of-distribution mechanism.
The validation protocol contains three predefined perturbation tests; corresponding accuracies were 92.8%, 90.9%, and 93.4%.
A separate validation team reproduced the reported tests.
limitations: The OOD mechanism missed flagging 73 of the 1,200 out-of-distribution documents (approx. 6%).
Operational robustness is bounded by the specific predefined perturbations, formatting variations, and OCR degradations tested.
